name: Machete Hopper-optimized mixed-precision GEMM kernel (CUTLASS-based)
bits: w4a16 (4-bit weights, FP16 activations) - same precision as Marlin but optimized for Hopper SM90
activation_scheme: FP16 activations, no quantization. Weights are INT4 with per-group FP16 scales. Dequantizes to FP16 in registers before tensor-core multiply, same as Marlin.
kernels: vLLM machete backend (AWQ and GPTQ paths)
notes: PROXY ENUM VALUE - DECLARED 2026-10-04: Machete is a KERNEL (CUTLASS-based, SM90/Hopper), not a format, filed under 'awq' because it serves AWQ-packed weights. Same defect shape as the Marlin record: a query for AWQ returns a kernel record, and a reader may treat Machete as a format. Worth stating plainly because Machete and Marlin produce IDENTICAL output precision (both FP16 x FP16 W4A16) while being different kernels for different architectures - if the enum is the only thing a reader has, Machete under 'awq' and Marlin under 'gptq' will look like two different precisions when they are the same one. REQUESTED ENUM ADDITION: a 'machete' value. Machete is the Hopper-optimized successor to Marlin for W4A16 quantization. Built on CUTLASS, it targets SM90 (Hopper) specifically. The GPTQModel repo references it as a kernel option alongside Marlin and Swordfish. KEY DISTINCTION: Machete and Marlin produce the same numerical results (both dequantize INT4 weights to FP16 before the multiply), but Machete is optimized for Hopper's tensor core architecture and memory hierarchy. On Hopper, Machete should be preferred over Marlin. The vLLM quantization docs list Machete as a supported backend for AWQ and GPTQ on Hopper. No independent quality delta recorded - the kernel is numerically equivalent to Marlin for the same quantized weights, so the Marlin quality figures apply. SELECTION LOGIC: vLLM uses Machete when the GPU is SM90 (Hopper) and the quantization method is AWQ or GPTQ. On Ampere/Ada, Marlin is used instead. This is a hardware-dependent kernel selection that is transparent to the user but affects performance significantly.
